description: Retrieve a time series showing when news coverage of a topic spiked, or how average tone shifted over time. Use mode "volume" for normalized coverage intensity (% of all global coverage per timestep). Use "volume_raw" for distinct matching-article counts per timestep and norm, the unsmoothed monitored-article denominator; smoothed counts are moving averages. Use mode "volume_with_articles" for the same signal plus the top articles that drove each spike — this is the primary signal-detection mode: a single call reveals both the spike and its cause, avoiding a follow-up gdelt_search_articles call. Use mode "tone" for average sentiment score per timestep (negative = hostile/fearful, positive = celebratory). Date resolution is inferred from returned intervals: 15 minutes or hours for short windows, days for longer ones. In volume_with_articles mode each timestep carries its first 3 article links and referenceCount, the number of references GDELT supplied (up to ten), not all matching articles; name timesteps' dates in points to get only those timesteps, each with its full supplied list. A response carries limit timesteps (default 10, cap 400); when more remain it returns nextOffset — pass it back as offset with otherwise identical inputs for the next page. Note: DOC API covers only the last 3 months.

endDatetime.description: End datetime in GDELT format YYYYMMDDHHMMSS — exactly 14 digits, no separators (e.g. 20240131235959). Must pair with startDatetime; supplying only one of the two is rejected.

limit.description: Maximum timesteps per page (default 10, cap 400). Larger counts clamp to 400 unless GDELT_CLAMP_LIMITS=false.

mode.description: Timeline mode: "volume" returns normalized coverage % per timestep, "volume_raw" returns distinct matching-article counts (moving averages when smoothed) and the unsmoothed monitored denominator norm, "volume_with_articles" returns volume plus top articles per spike (best for signal detection), "tone" returns average sentiment score per timestep.

offset.description: Zero-based timestep offset — into the timeline, or into the timesteps named in points. Pass nextOffset from the preceding response, with otherwise identical inputs, to get the next page.

points.description: Timestep dates to return alone, e.g. ["2024-01-05T12:00:00Z"]. Take them verbatim from series[].data[].date in a prior response, or from the list an unknown_point error prints. The response then carries only these timesteps, in timeline order, and in volume_with_articles mode each carries its complete article list instead of the first 3. A date matching no timestep is rejected rather than silently ignored.

query.description: Search query using GDELT syntax. Same operators as gdelt_search_articles: phrases, boolean OR, sourcecountry:, sourcelang:, domain:, theme: (GKG theme identifiers come from gdelt_search_themes), tone<.

smoothing.description: Trailing moving-average width in timesteps (0–30; 0 or 1 leaves values unsmoothed). Width N needs N source steps, omitting leading steps without a full window and potentially shifting peaks later.

startDatetime.description: Start datetime in GDELT format YYYYMMDDHHMMSS — exactly 14 digits, no separators (e.g. 20240101000000). Must pair with endDatetime; supplying only one of the two is rejected.

timespan.description: Time window relative to now, minimum "15min"; other examples: "24h", "7d", "1m". Ignored when startDatetime/endDatetime are set. Maximum 3 months.

name: gdelt_get_coverage_timeline

dateResolution.description: Temporal resolution of the data points — 15min, hour, or day — inferred from the spacing of the returned timesteps. Omitted when fewer than two distinct timesteps came back.

effectiveQuery.description: Echoed query string for use in follow-up calls.

error.description: Present when the call failed. Absent on success.

code.description: JSON-RPC error code for this failure.

reason.description: Machine-readable failure mode. Declared by this tool: `unknown_point`: A date passed in the points input matches no timestep in a non-empty timeline. `offset_out_of_range`: The requested offset is at or beyond the last timestep of a non-empty timeline, or of the timesteps named in points. `invalid_date_range`: Only one of startDatetime / endDatetime was supplied, one of them is not a real UTC calendar timestamp, or startDatetime is not earlier than endDatetime. `invalid_query`: GDELT rejected the query string as malformed — bad keyword length, unbalanced parentheses, or an illegal character. `gdelt_rate_limited`: GDELT rejected the request for its one-request-per-five-seconds limit, or too many requests were already queued for this one to start in time. `gdelt_unavailable`: GDELT DOC API is unreachable or temporarily returned no usable data. Other values are possible when a failure originates below the handler.

recovery.description: Actionable next step for the caller.

message.description: Human-readable description of what went wrong.

expandedPoints.description: Timestep dates this response is restricted to, each carrying its full article list — echoing the points input. Omitted when points was not supplied.

limitClamp.description: Present only when the requested count exceeded the per-call cap: the call ran exactly as a call at the cap, and every count, notice, and continuation in this response reflects the applied value.

applied.description: The per-call cap the call ran with instead.

parameter.description: The count input that was clamped.

requested.description: The value the call asked for.

mode.description: Timeline mode used for this response.

nextOffset.description: Offset of the next page, for the same inputs. Absent when this page reaches the last timestep.

notice.description: Guidance when the query matched no coverage in the window — how to broaden the query or extend the window — or, when this response is one page of several, which timesteps it returned out of how many. Absent when the whole timeline fit in one response.

series.description: One or more time series (typically one for volume/tone), holding the timesteps of this page.

items.description: A single time series with a label and data points.

data.description: Time-ordered data points of this series returned in this response.

articles.description: Top articles driving coverage at this timestep — the first 3, or all of them for a timestep named in points. Present only in volume_with_articles mode.

items.description: An article linked to this spike.

norm.description: Total articles monitored at this timestep, unsmoothed even when value is smoothed. Present only in volume_raw mode.

referenceCount.description: Number of article references GDELT supplied for this timestep (up to ten), not all matching articles; articles carries the first 3 unless the timestep was named in points. Present whenever articles is.

value.description: Normalized coverage % (volume or volume_with_articles), distinct matching-article count (volume_raw; a moving average when smoothed), or average tone score (tone mode). Tone range is approximately -100 to +100.

peak.description: The point of the whole series with the largest absolute value, across every page — it may lie outside data. Omitted when the series has no points.

date.description: Timestep of the peak, in ISO 8601 format.

norm.description: Unsmoothed monitored-article denominator at the peak in volume_raw mode.

pointCount.description: Data points in the whole series, across every page — not only those in data. Present whenever the series has points.

totalCount.description: Total number of data points across all series of the full timeline, not this page.

title: Get GDELT Coverage Timeline
